title: Eine Pilotstudie zur Bewertung der Machbarkeit und Validierung des Remote-Reportings durch Betreuungspersonen sowie eine Kosten-Effizienz-Analyse des Teledentistry-Assessments bei Kontrollbesuchen bei Kindern
summary:
Background
Many children need to visit the dental clinic for a follow-up appointment after a treatment or a dental injury. In many cases, it turns out that everything has healed well and the physical visit was not actually necessary. At the same time, new technologies allow the transmission of information and images from a distance.

Research Question
We want to find out if it is possible and reliable to conduct certain follow-up examinations for children remotely. The study aims to determine if the information sent by parents via an app (photos, videos, and questionnaires) is sufficient for the dentist to decide whether a clinic visit is truly necessary or if the remote assessment is enough. We also want to investigate whether this saves time and money for families and how satisfied parents, children, and dentists are with this method.

Methodology: Approximately 40 children who require a routine follow-up will participate in the study. The process is as follows:
Caregivers send standardized information and photos or videos of the tooth or mouth to the clinic using an app. The dentist evaluates this information remotely and decides if a visit to the clinic is necessary from their perspective. Regardless of this remote assessment, the child will still come for a scheduled appointment at the clinic so that the dentist can perform a direct physical examination.By comparing the remote assessment with the in-person examination, we will check how accurate this method is. Additionally, parents and children will complete short questionnaires to share their opinions on this new approach.

interventions.name: Systemically healthy children and adolescents recruited from our regularly scheduled patients, who are scheduled for a routine procedure re-evaluation or a standard clinical follow-up assessment following dental trauma in accordance with established clinical guidelines for post-intervention monitori

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Children & adolescents (< 18 years old) 
- Children, who received clinical procedures (e.g. minor oral surgeries performed under local anaesthesia, placement of fixed space maintainers) in the last 6 weeks or standard follow-up related to dental trauma (including primary teeth trauma or mild permanent teeth trauma), which under normal circumstances typically does not require treatment but follow-up assessment within 6 weeks. 
- Children & adolescents without systematic health diseases with an agreement to voluntary study participation  
-Willing to participate in the teledentistry assessment and in the in-person appointment.
Exclusion criteria:
- Patients with acute pain / irreversible pulpitis or symptoms to be treated.  
- Patients with systemic disease that require special attention during their dental treatment.  
- Patients & guardians denying to participate immediate reassessment using photo, phone call or video-call if it’s required. 
- Patients & caregivers with language barriers.
